title: Exercise Northstar: D-7
description: One week out. Stress testing shows the command screen crashes when more than 500 users connect at once. The exercise will have 3,000. Time to fix this before the generals notice.
storyContext: One week out. Stress test results: the command screen crashes at 500 users. The exercise will have 3,000. Your team lead slides the report across the table: "The generals demo this on Thursday. Fix it or we explain to a two-star why his screen went blank."

software-engineer.title: Fix the Overload
software-engineer.instruction: The screen works for 500 users but crashes at 3,000. Each user currently gets their own private data stream — 3,000 streams all fighting for the same resources. How do you fix it?
software-engineer.hint: When too many people share a limited resource, either make them share smarter or add more of that resource. Which can you do in 7 days?

options.label: Group users so 50 share one data stream instead of getting their own. Cuts load by 95% but adds a 1-second delay.
Add more identical machines and spread users evenly. Each handles 500 comfortably. More expensive but needs zero changes in 7 days.
Rewrite the connection system so one machine handles thousands at once. Could support 10,000 users — but it's a big rewrite with 7 days left.
Generals get live updates, officers get 10-second delays, everyone else gets 30-second snapshots. Cuts live connections to under 200.

data-scientist.title: Estimate Peak Users
data-scientist.instruction: Not all 3,000 log in at once. The graph shows the peak simultaneous users from each previous exercise (in hundreds). Estimate the peak for this one.
data-scientist.hint: Look at how the peak grows from exercise to exercise. Is it linear or accelerating? Where does the pattern land next?

cloud-engineer.title: Run the Stress Test
cloud-engineer.instruction: Before fixing the crash, you need to understand every breaking point. Arrange the test steps.
cloud-engineer.hint: Every good test starts by recording what normal looks like. Then push until it breaks, and figure out why.

items.label: Record normal performance with 100 simulated users as a baseline
Gradually increase to 500 users — note where things slow down
Push past 500 to find the exact moment it breaks and how
Check machine load, memory, and network at the breaking point
Apply the fix, then run the full test again from scratch
